h03.

The provider abstraction lives in the `idp` package at `internal/idp` (file `internal/idp/idp.go`), and the single concrete protocol implementation that ships is the OAuth2 provider in `internal/idp/oauth2` (file `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`).

**Answer: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go`); `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`)**

Details worth noting:

- The abstraction is deliberately thin — `internal/idp/idp.go` contains only the normalized user shape that any provider must produce, with no Go interface type:

```1:8:internal/idp/idp.go
package idp

type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {
	Identifier  string
	DisplayName string
	Email       string
	AvatarURL   string
```

The browser hits `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`, which is served by the file server (not the gRPC API) and reaches the `user.avatar_url` column; the image bytes are stored inline as a base64 data URI in that column rather than as a file on disk or in object storage.

**Answer:**

```
Route registration: fileGroup.GET("/file/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124
serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
(*FileServerService).getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
(*Store).GetUser — store/user.go:148
(*Store).ListUsers — store/user.go:136
store.Driver.ListUsers (interface dispatch to active driver) — store/user.go:137
(*DB).ListUsers, e.g. SQLite — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?, store/db/sqlite/user.go:150-165)
(*FileServerService).parseDataURI — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:196 (decodes user.AvatarURL to bytes)
```

Supporting notes on each hop:

- **How the browser learns the URL.** The API doesn't ship the base64 blob in JSON. `convertUserFromStore` rewrites the field to a file-server path when the stored value is inline image data (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:31-40`):

```32:38:server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go
	if user.AvatarURL != "" {
		// Check if avatar url is base64 format.
		_, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL)
		if err == nil {
			userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name)
		} else {
			userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL
		}
```

Since `userpb.Name` is `BuildUserName(user.Username)` (i.e. `users/{username}`), the emitted path is exactly `/file/users/{username}/avatar`, matching the registered route. If the stored value is an external URL instead, it's passed through and no server hop happens at all.

- **Handler.** `serveUserAvatar` first gates anonymous access: on a private instance (`!s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()`) it requires a session, access token, or PAT via `getCurrentUser`, returning 401 otherwise (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:173-181`). There is no per-user authorization beyond that, so any permitted viewer can fetch any other user's avatar.

- **Lookup hop.** The `:identifier` path segment is treated as a username, wrapped into a `FindUser`:

```715:717:server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
func (s *FileServerService) getUserByUsername(ctx context.Context, identifier string) (*store.User, error) {
	return s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})
```

h14.

The derived metadata is the memo's `payload.tags` and `payload.property`, computed by a single markdown AST walk. It's written only by `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload`, which the API calls on memo creation and on content updates — nothing else in production writes those fields.

**Answer: computation site — `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`), delegating the actual extraction to `(*service).ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`); triggers — `CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`) and `UpdateMemo` when the update mask includes `content` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`), plus the unused bulk backfill `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`); extracted properties — deduplicated `#tags`, and the `Property` fields `has_link`, `has_code`, `has_task_list`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, and `title` (first H1 heading).**

The writer is small and is the only place these fields are assigned:

```74:88:server/runner/memopayload/runner.go
func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
	if memo.Payload == nil {
		memo.Payload = &storepb.MemoPayload{}
	}

	// Use goldmark service to extract all metadata in a single pass (more efficient)
	data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
	if err != nil {
		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to extract markdown metadata")
	}

	memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
	memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
	return nil
}
```

A grep for assignments to `Payload.Tags` or `Payload.Property` across `server/`, `store/`, and `internal/` returns only lines 85 and 86 above, confirming there's no second computation path.

What `ExtractAll` derives during its single `gast.Walk` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356-421`):

| Output | Rule |
|---|---|
| `Tags` | every `#tag` node, deduplicated preserving original case |
| `Property.HasLink` | any `gast.KindLink` node |
| `Property.HasCode` | any code block, fenced code block, or inline code span |
| `Property.HasTaskList` | any task checkbox |
| `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` | any task checkbox with `IsChecked == false` |
| `Property.Title` | text of the first block-level child of the document, only if it is a level-1 heading |

It also collects `Mentions` in the same pass, but `RebuildMemoPayload` discards that field — mentions are consumed separately for notifications via `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32`.

On triggers, two details matter. Creation runs the rebuild before the insert, after the content-length check, and location is layered onto the payload afterward (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:101-113`). Update only recomputes inside the `path == "content"` branch of the update-mask loop, and the refreshed payload is attached to the store update alongside the new content (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:439-453`); changing visibility, pinned state, or location therefore leaves the derived metadata untouched, which is correct since none of them affect content-derived values. The third trigger, `Runner.RunOnce`, would rebuild every memo in batches of 100, but its constructor `memopayload.NewRunner` has no call sites, so it never executes in a running server.

On the consumption side, the stored values are surfaced to clients by `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:315-326`), wired in at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:49`. Note that the list/preview `snippet` field is a separate, non-persisted value computed per response from `memo.Content` via `getMemoContentSnippet` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76-80`), not part of this stored payload. The schema for these fields is `proto/store/memo.proto:12-22`.

```
checkAttachmentAccess (API attachment read, via parent memo visibility) — server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422 (checks at :445, :451)

CreateMemoComment parent-memo check — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20 (check at :41)
checkAttachmentPermission (file server binary serving, incl. share-token bypass) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650 (checks at :677, :699)
SSEClient.canReceive (server-side event delivery filter) — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134
RSS feed queries pinned to PUBLIC — server/router/rss/rss.go:90 (GetExploreRSS) and server/router/rss/rss.go:141 (GetUserRSS)
Sitemap query pinned to PUBLIC — server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150 (getSitemapXML)
canViewerAccessMemo (notification content gating) — server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:302 and server/notification/email.go:306; mention variant canUserAccessMentionContext — server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:56
```

Notes on the shape of each mechanism:

- **The canonical gate** handles archived memos and the three visibility levels, returning `NotFound` for archived non-owners, `Unauthenticated` for anonymous access to non-public memos, and `PermissionDenied` for private memos owned by someone else:

```55:66:server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go
	if memo.Visibility != store.Public {
		user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user")
		}
		if user == nil {
			return status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")
		}
		if memo.Visibility == store.Private && memo.CreatorID != user.ID {
			return status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
		}
	}
```

- **Listing is enforced in the query, not post-filtered.** Anonymous callers get `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]`; authenticated callers get a CEL filter `creator_id == N || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]`, or `[PUBLIC, PROTECTED]` when browsing another specific user (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227`).

- **The file server is the one surface with a bypass.** Beyond the usual checks it honors a `share_token` query parameter, granting access to private/protected memos' attachments when the token is unexpired and issued for that exact memo (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:684-690`). It also requires `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` before serving even public attachments anonymously (`:677`). The matching API-level share path is `GetMemoByShare` with `getActiveMemoShare` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go:153`, `:199`).

- **SSE filters on the way out**, per subscribed client: private-memo events go only to the creator or an admin, while public, protected, and unset visibility are broadcast, and unknown values are denied (`server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134-144`).

- **The four inline API checks** (attachments, list-attachments, reactions read/write, comment creation) repeat the same shape as `checkMemoReadAccess` but add `isSuperUser(user)` as an escape hatch, which the central gate does not have — a real behavioral difference between the sites.

- **RSS and the sitemap** enforce by construction rather than by check, hardcoding `VisibilityList: []store.Visibility{store.Public}` in their `FindMemo`, so non-public memos never enter those responses.

- **Notification gating** is arguably a different concern than request authorization, but it does re-derive viewer access from memo visibility before including memo content in emails/inbox messages, and there are two near-duplicate `canViewerAccessMemo` implementations (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:302` and `server/notification/email.go:306`) plus the mention-specific variant.

One thing I did not find: the MCP surface has no visibility logic of its own. Its catalog exposes `MemoService_ListMemos` and `MemoService_GetMemo` (`server/router/mcp/catalog.go:12-14`) and dispatches into the same API v1 handlers, so it inherits the enforcement above rather than duplicating it.

value.text:
r01.

There is no Redis anywhere in this repository — the premise doesn't hold. A case-insensitive search for "redis" across all files (Go sources, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, Docker/compose files, configs, docs) returns zero matches, so there is no Redis connection to configure and no external cache server involved.

**Actual mechanism: the cache layer is a process-local, in-memory cache implemented in `store/cache/cache.go`, and user entries use the default 10-minute TTL configured once in `store/store.go:40-45`.**

Details:

- **What the cache actually is.** `cache.Cache` is a thread-safe in-memory store built on `sync.Map` plus an atomic item counter, with per-entry expiration timestamps (`store/cache/cache.go:66-73`). It's created by `cache.New`, which spawns a background `cleanupLoop` goroutine (`store/cache/cache.go:76-85`, `:200-215`). Nothing is serialized or sent over a network; the data lives in the server process, so it is not shared across replicas.

- **Where it's "configured."** In code, not in any connection string or config file. `store.New` builds one `cache.Config` and hands the same values to three separate cache instances:

```39:53:store/store.go
	// Default cache settings
	cacheConfig := cache.Config{
		DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
		CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
		MaxItems:        1000,
		OnEviction:      nil,
	}

	store := &Store{
		driver:               driver,
		profile:              profile,
		cacheConfig:          cacheConfig,
		instanceSettingCache: cache.New(cacheConfig),
		userCache:            cache.New(cacheConfig),
		userSettingCache:     cache.New(cacheConfig),
```

These values are hardcoded — there is no flag, environment variable, or setting that overrides them. `cache.DefaultConfig()` (`store/cache/cache.go:57-64`) declares the identical defaults, though `store.New` specifies its own copy rather than calling it.

- **The TTL for user entries: 10 minutes.** All user writes go through `Set`, never `SetWithTTL` (a search for `SetWithTTL` outside the cache package itself returns no hits), and `Set` applies the configured default:

```92:95:store/cache/cache.go
// Set adds a value to the cache with the default TTL.
func (c *Cache) Set(ctx context.Context, key string, value any) {
	c.SetWithTTL(ctx, key, value, c.config.DefaultTTL)
}
```

Call sites populating the user cache are `store/user.go:98`, `:122`, `:132`, `:143`, and `:167`, keyed by `userCacheKey(user.ID)` (`store/user.go:88`).

- **How expiry is realized.** Two ways: lazily on read, where `Get` deletes and reports a miss for an expired item (`store/cache/cache.go:135-144`), and proactively by the cleanup goroutine every 5 minutes (`store/cache/cache.go:218-250`). There's also a capacity bound — once the instance exceeds 1000 items, `cleanupOldest` drops roughly 20% of `MaxItems` (`store/cache/cache.go:117-119`, `:253-313`), so user entries can be evicted before their TTL expires.

- **Invalidation beyond TTL.** User deletion explicitly removes the entry (`store/user_delete.go:40`), and shutdown stops the cleanup goroutines via `Store.Close` (`store/store.go:74-76`). Note that lookups only consult the cache when finding by ID (`store/user.go:149-156`); username or email lookups always hit the database.

r02.

The premise is incorrect: there is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware in this repository, so there is nothing registered and no request limits to report.

Evidence for the absence:

- A case-insensitive search across all Go files for `ratelimit`, `rate_limit`, "rate limit", `throttl`, `limiter`, and `golang.org/x/time/rate` produces exactly one hit, and it is an aspirational comment in package documentation rather than an implementation: `internal/email/doc.go:86` lists "Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse" as a future consideration.
- `go.mod` contains no rate-limiting dependency (no `golang.org/x/time`, no `echo` rate-limiter package, nothing matching `rate`/`limit`/`throttl`).
- The full set of middleware registered on the Echo server is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`, with the CORS config at `server/cors.go:14`), plus static-file and SPA-fallback middleware for the frontend (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54`, `:59`). No limiter is in that chain. Request authorization happens in the gateway middleware and Connect interceptor set up in `RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65`), which authenticates but does not count or throttle requests.
- There is also no login-attempt throttling or account lockout; searching the auth code for "attempt", "lockout", "backoff", and "too many" only turns up comments and a result struct name (`server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:277`, `server/auth/authenticator.go:126`).

What does exist, in case one of these is what you were thinking of — these are concurrency and size bounds, not per-user request rates:

- **Concurrency semaphores for expensive media work:** thumbnail generation is capped at 3 concurrent operations in the file server (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:45-46`, `:116`) and at 3 in the API service, with image processing capped at 2 (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`). These are global caps, not per-user.
- **Pagination cap:** list responses are clamped to `MaxPageSize = 1000` (`server/router/api/v1/common.go:17`).
- **Bounded webhook dispatch queue:** outbound webhooks go onto a 128-slot channel drained by 4 workers, and payloads are dropped when it's full (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55`, `:184-196`).
- **SSE backpressure:** events for slow clients are dropped rather than blocking the hub (`server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:126-131`).
- **Content size limit:** memo content length is checked against an instance setting on create and update (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:101-107`, `:442-449`).

r03.

The premise is incorrect on two counts: there is no nightly database-cleanup job anywhere in the codebase, and the cron scheduler that exists is never used by the running server — no production code imports it, so it has no registered jobs at all.

Evidence:

- **The scheduler is unwired.** `internal/scheduler` implements a full cron system (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, with a five-field cron parser in `internal/scheduler/parser.go`, job types in `internal/scheduler/job.go`, and middleware in `internal/scheduler/middleware.go`), but a search for the import path `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler` returns only two hits, both inside the package's own tests: `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10` and `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`. Neither `cmd/`, `server/`, nor `store/` references it, so `scheduler.New`, `Register`, and `Start` never run in a live server.

- **No cleanup job exists to schedule.** The only cron-looking strings in non-test Go code are illustrative comments, not registrations: `"0 * * * *"` / `"0 0 * * *"` as examples in `internal/scheduler/job.go:21`, and `Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily` in the package doc example at `internal/scheduler/doc.go:16`. That 2 AM value is documentation for how to write a job, not a configured job. Searching for cleanup/nightly/cron terms across `server/`, `cmd/`, and `store/` turns up only unrelated things: inline resource cleanup during memo and user deletion (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:579`, `server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:421-450`), best-effort SSO rollback (`server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:76`), and test teardown helpers (`server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:65`).

What actually runs on a schedule in the server, none of it cron-driven and none of it database cleanup:

- **The S3 presign runner**, the only background runner started at boot: one immediate pass plus a `time.Ticker` every 12 hours, refreshing presigned attachment URLs (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41`, wired at `server/server.go:161-171`).
- **In-memory cache eviction**, a per-cache goroutine ticking every 5 minutes to drop expired entries (`store/cache/cache.go:60`, `:200-215`). This evicts process memory, not database rows.

There is also a second unused runner, `memopayload.Runner`, whose `RunOnce` would rebuild all memo payloads in batches, but its constructor has no call sites (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:19`).
